subject: Temporary proxy subprocessor swap — DPA addendum & contracts action
messages:
From: Lena Morgan <lena.morgan@oakside.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@oakside.com
Date: 2027-02-14 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Question on transient proxy provider change and evidence

Hi Irene,

Quick one — we received a notice from one of our partners flagging that Redwood will be routing telemetry through a short-term proxy partner (named ProxyFlow) next week for two maintenance windows (2/17 and 2/18). Can you confirm:

- Is this going to touch log/telemetry for Oakside prod customers?
- Is ProxyFlow a persistent subprocessor or a temporary bridge?
- Can you share the subprocessor notice + any SOC2/KMS attestations for ProxyFlow?

Procurement is also asking whether this change requires a DPA addendum or an internal approval cycle. Can you advise on timing? We need to make sure our compliance review closes before the scheduled maintenance.

Appreciate a short note or the relevant docs.

Thanks,
Lena Morgan
Sr. Security Manager
Oakside Finance

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Morgan <lena.morgan@oakside.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-02-14 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Question on transient proxy provider change and evidence

Hi Lena — thanks for the ping and great questions. Short answer up front: this is a temporary transit proxy we will use for two scheduled maintenance windows only; it is a transient subprocessor (not a long-term change), and we have attached the short notice and a DPA addendum draft for your review.

Details:
- Scope: ProxyFlow will only handle aggregated telemetry and routing metadata during the maintenance windows. No customer content or model inputs/outputs are routed to ProxyFlow.
- Duration: 02/17 22:00 UTC — 02/18 04:00 UTC and a backup window 02/18 22:00 UTC — 02/19 02:00 UTC.
- Controls: ProxyFlow is contractually limited to ephemeral buffering and TLS-encrypted transit. They do not persist logs for more than 48 hours; we have required HMAC attestations and minimal access clauses in the addendum.

Attachments I am sending: subprocessor_change_notice.pdf (formal notice) and dpa_addendum_v1.docx (draft addendum with minimal-scope text).

Action items we need from Oakside:
1) Confirmation whether Oakside requires a countersigned DPA addendum (DocuSign) or whether acknowledgment by email is sufficient.
2) If countersign required: please confirm point of contact in procurement/legal and timeline (we aim to get this signed before 02/16 EOD PT).

Kimberly and Marissa are looped for any legal/procurement follow-up; Kimberly — any immediate redlines you want me to flag back to Oakside? Marissa — FYI from CS side in case this touches any renewal timelines.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Manager, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, Lena Morgan <lena.morgan@oakside.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-02-14 12:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Question on transient proxy provider change and evidence

Hi all — quick read-through attached. High-level notes for Oakside:

- We consider ProxyFlow a transient/temporary subprocessor used only for transit; the DPA addendum is narrowly scoped and only adds the transit subprocessor clause plus the short retention & encryption assurances.
- Key redlines we suggest (we can incorporate before DocuSign): a) explicit non-persistence clause (48h max), b) restricted purpose language (transit only; no analytics), c) right-to-audit limited to sampled configs with 48h notice.
- We do not expect SOC2 Type II from ProxyFlow for this short-lived bridge; instead we required a short attestation package and contractual data-handling obligations. If Oakside requires SOC2 evidence we need to know immediately as that will push the timeline and likely block the 02/17 maintenance window.

Irene — I've added a few tracked comments in dpa_addendum_v1.docx and flagged a DocuSign template that we can use to speed countersign.

Lena — please advise whether your legal/procurement needs the SOC2 or if the attestation and contractual addendum are sufficient.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Lena and Oakside procurement team — following up with concrete next steps so we don't block the maintenance window.

1) Attached is the formal notice (subprocessor_change_notice.pdf) and the DPA addendum with Kimberly's comments incorporated (dpa_addendum_v1.docx).
2) If Oakside is fine with an acknowledged notice (no countersign), please reply to this thread with confirmation by 02/16 17:00 PT.
3) If countersign required: we have preloaded the DocuSign envelope and can send it immediately; sign-off deadline for 02/17 maintenance is 02/16 17:00 PT to allow internal review. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/en/status/ABC12345

We also included a brief attestation from ProxyFlow (kept internal per their terms) confirming 48-hour retention, TLS-only transit, and access restrictions. If Oakside's security team requires additional evidence (SOC2), please escalate now — otherwise the attestation + contractual addendum will be the deliverable.

Thanks for the fast turnaround — happy to hop on a 15m call if that helps (Irene/Kimberly available 02/15 afternoon).

Best,
Irene Choi
